methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a local native in Hampton Roads represent grassroots capability-building outside major tech hubs, signaling potential for peer-driven distributed fluency if these efforts scale beyond one-off training events.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's formal partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates institutional AI expertise and resources in the Richmond metro area, deepening capabilities in an existing urban center rather than distributing them across Virginia's rural regions.

signals.title: Children’s National and Virginia Tech deepen pediatric AI collaboration to accelerate innovation for children - Children's National Hospital
signals.signal_reading: Children's National and Virginia Tech collaboration creates a deep technical partnership between established research institutions, concentrating pediatric AI innovation capacity in areas with existing university infrastructure rather than broader community access.

signals.title: Tony Stark’s J.A.R.V.I.S., meet Amelia, Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s IT AI help assistant - MilitaryNews.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard's deployment of Amelia, an AI IT help assistant, represents platform-delivered AI adoption that enables broad usage without requiring deep technical expertise from end users, creating shallow but functional AI integration in defense-adjacent workforce.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ investment in AI data center infrastructure in Henrico concentrates physical and economic AI resources in the Richmond metro corridor, reinforcing capital flows to existing tech growth areas while creating primarily operational rather than innovation-focused jobs.
